one_line: Overseer of Budshah’s Naushahr madrasa and translation bureau in 15th‑century Srinagar.

appearance.age_look: late 40s to early 50s, medium height, slight stoop from years of study, lean but not frail
appearance.face: oval face with a high thoughtful forehead, medium wheatish Kashmiri complexion, neatly trimmed black beard with a few grey strands at the chin, straight nose, calm deep-set eyes with soft crow’s feet, default expression a gentle, focused half-smile as if listening and explaining at once
appearance.hair: dark black hair streaked subtly with grey, kept short and tidy beneath a soft white Kashmiri-style turban wrapped simply with a flat top and one narrow tail folded over the left shoulder; no visible loose hair except a short fringe at the temples
appearance.costume: era-accurate scholar’s attire: a long-sleeved knee-length Persian-influenced robe (jama) in muted indigo cotton with a simple round neck and front opening tied by small fabric loops, worn over a light cream ankle-length tunic and narrow cream trousers; a sleeveless olive-green woollen waistcoat (sadri) with side vents, no ornament except a subtle woven border; a wide rust-red woollen shawl draped over both shoulders and wrapped once around the torso, the ends hanging at the front; soft brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes; a slim leather belt at the waist carrying a small cloth pouch and a simple brass inkpot hanging from a cord
appearance.signature: a well-used rectangular wooden writing board held in his left hand, with a partially unrolled light-brown paper folio clipped to it and a dark reed pen in his right hand poised as if annotating a Sanskrit verse in Persian script, the board’s edge carved with a small geometric border

ref_desc: Maulana Kabir is a late‑middle‑aged Kashmiri scholar with a short dark beard, simple white turban, indigo robe over cream garments, olive waistcoat, rust shawl, brown shoes and a wooden writing board with reed pen as his constant scholarly prop.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character of Maulana Kabir as a dignified 15th-century Kashmiri scholar in Budshah’s Naushahr: late-middle-aged, lean, wheatish complexion, oval face, calm deep-set eyes, short neatly trimmed dark beard with a few grey strands, and a simple white turban with a flat top and one tail folded over his left shoulder. His exact costume is a muted indigo long-sleeved knee-length robe (jama) over a light cream ankle-length tunic and narrow cream trousers, with a sleeveless olive-green wool waistcoat and a wide rust-red wool shawl draped over both shoulders and wrapped once around his torso, plus soft brown slightly upturned leather shoes and a slim leather belt with a small pouch and brass inkpot. He holds a rectangular wooden writing board with a clipped light-brown paper folio in his left hand and a dark reed pen poised in his right, ready to annotate, with the board’s edge carved in a simple geometric border. Show him standing in a neutral pose, front-facing, so his face, turban, layered garments, shawl, shoes, belt accessories, and the writing board with pen are all clearly visible in consistent indigo, cream, olive green, rust red, and brown tones.
